THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2023:KHC:44363  WP No. 5389 of 2023  C/W WP No. 844 of 2023  ORDER W.P.no.5389/2023 is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(i) Issue a writ of mandamus or any writ or directing third respondent to consider representation vide Annexure-K dated 27.02.2023.

(ii) In alternative direct respondent authorities to pay compensation in accordance with New Act of 2013 etc.
2.

Sri K. Suresh Desai, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner is grandson of Siddamma who was issued a grant certificate to extent of 1 acre 30 guntas in Sy.no.112 of Jyothipura village, Mandur Post, under order dated 17.06.1997 issued by Tahsildar, Bengaluru South Taluk.

It was submitted that said land was notified by respondent no.1 for acquisition for benefit of respondent no.3 by issuing Preliminary Notification under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act,
Venkataramanappa vs Principal Secretary on 7 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183945986/
3 1984 (for short, 'Act') on 11.03.2010.

entities.text: Venkataramanappa vs Principal Secretary on 7 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was submitted that said notification was by invoking urgency clause under Section 17(1)(4) of Act at Annexure-H, which imposed pre- condition upon beneficiary to deposit cost of acquisition.

It was submitted that on account of non-deposit of cost of acquisition,
acquisition process initiated in pursuance of Preliminary NC: 2023:KHC:44363 Notification dated 11.03.2010 could not be completed and consequently acquisition lapsed.

3. It was submitted that petitioner's grandmother earlier filed W.P.no.5611/2011 praying for direction to consider petitioner's representation dated 15.09.2011 etc., wherein request was made to SLAO to acquire petitioner's property by passing award.

It was submitted that in said writ petition,
this Court observed that respondent no.3 was in possession, but writ petition was disposed of with clarification that acquisition in pursuance of Preliminary Notification dated 11.03.2010 stood lapsed and liberty was reserved to petitioner to take steps for getting back possession of proposed land.
Liberty was also reserved to respondents to initiate fresh acquisition proceedings.
However, no fresh acquisition proceedings were initiated while respondent had continued in possession illegally.

Therefore, representation at Annexure-K dated 27.02.2023 was filed seeking for deposit of acquisition cost and for passing award in name of interested person etc.
4.

In response, respondent no.3 has filed statement of objections stating that land bearing Sy.no.112 of Jyothipura NC: 2023:KHC:44363 Village, Mandur Post was already notified and acquired in favour of respondent in year 1993 and 1995 as item no.15 in Annexure-R1 and item no.11 in Annexure-R2.

It is stated that for said acquisition, respondent no.3 had deposited a sum of Rs.3.3 Crores on 31.10.1991 as per Annexure-R3 and Rs.2,48,00,000/- deposited by cheque dated 04.01.1993 as per Annexures-R7 and R8.
A further sum of Rs.1 Crore was deposited on 11.06.1966 as per Annexures-R10 and R11.
Thus respondent had deposited entire amount towards acquisition of land.

5. It was submitted that a total extent of 746 acres and 3 guntas spread over 6 villages in Jyothipura,
Sringaripura, Katgullahalli, Thirumallenahalli, Handarahalli and Chalamakunte were acquired and handed over to Defense Department namely-DRDO in year 1993.

It was contended that entire acquisition had proceeded in accordance with law and stood concluded much prior to issuance of acquisition notification dated 11.03.2010.
6.

It was submitted that in earlier writ petition filed by petitioner's grandmother, this Court had clarified that if NC: 2023:KHC:44363 petitioner was forcibly dispossessed, it was open for her to take steps for getting back possession.
Under circumstances, there was no cause as contended in representation and therefore, no relief could be granted in this writ petition.

It was also contended that relief sought in earlier writ petition was also for consideration of representation for payment of compensation and therefore similar relief could not be sought once again in respect of said land, on same ground.

7. It was further contended that entire claim for compensation was with reference to acquisition proceedings initiated in pursuance of notification dated 11.03.2010 which was already held to have lapsed by this Court.

Therefore, petitioner could not make any claim for compensation except right to recover possession of property, in case they were illegally dispossessed and sought for dismissal of Venkataramanappa vs Principal Secretary on 7 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183945986/
4 writ petition.
8.
Learned AGA sought to contend that since basis for petitioner's claim rested on a grant of year 1997 which was after acquisition of land, petitioner would not be entitled for compensation.

In reply, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that acquisition sought to be relied upon by respondent in year 1993 and 1995 was not in respect of land bearing Sy.no.112/P33 and therefore,
respondents claim that petitioner's land was acquired earlier was factually is correct.
It was submitted that as per observation in earlier writ petition admittedly respondents had continued in possession, if same was without acquisition, respondents would be liable to pay compensation.

10. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition records.
11.
From above, it is seen that main grievance of petitioner is non-payment of compensation for illegal dispossession and its continuation.
Admittedly, petitioner was granted 1 acres 30 guntas of land in bearing Sy.no.112 as per Annexure-C.

While petitioner contend that as per communication issued, respondent no.3 had failed to deposit compensation for acquisition initiated in pursuance of Preliminary Notification dated 11.03.2010 and therefore respondent no.3 was in illegal possession of petitioner's land without acquisition.
NC: 2023:KHC:44363 12.
Respondents on other hand, contend that land bearing Sy.no.112 of Jyothipura Village was acquired under earlier acquisition proceedings and therefore was not required to be notified.

Therefore, acquisition in pursuance of notification dated 11.03.2010 was rightly abandoned and since it had already deposited compensation in pursuance of earlier acquisition, petitioner could not have any claim against respondent no.3.
13.

On perusal of acquisition notifications at Annexures- R1 and R2, it is seen that land bearing Sy.no.112 of Jyothipura village was notified for acquisition for purposes of respondent no.3 in year 1993 and 1995.
It is also seen from Annexures-R3 to R10 that respondent no.3-DRDO had deposited amounts with SLAO, Bengaluru South Taluk towards acquisition.

Thus, it appears that land bearing Sy.no.112 of Jyothipura village was subject matter of acquisition much earlier to notification dated 11.03.2010 which would prima facie justify respondent no.3 being in possession.

14. Whether acquisition proceedings have been validly concluded in pursuance of earlier acquisition proceedings would - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:44363 be a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided in present context especially when petitioner's claim is for compensation.

Thus, there would be no justification for Venkataramanappa vs Principal Secretary on 7 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183945986/
5 petitioner to pursue remedies in pursuance of Annexure-K.

sentences.text: However, in case petitioner makes an appropriate representation or application to LAO seeking for disbursal of compensation on basis of issuance of saguvali chit at Annexure- C, respondent no.2 is directed to consider same in accordance with law.
15. For said purposes, liberty is reserved to respondent no.2 to seek clarification / documents from petitioner.
Respondent no.2 to inform to petitioner of result of consideration.
Petitioner is at liberty to give a representation to respondent no.2 within a period of four weeks from today.
Thereafter, respondent no.2 to consider same and pass appropriate orders within six months.

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:44363 (i) Issue a writ of mandamus or any writ or directing third respondent to consider representation vide Annexures-J and K dated 11.05.2021 and 05.01.2023.
(ii) In alternative direct respondent authorities to pay compensation in accordance with New Act of 2013 etc.
2.

Sri K. Suresh Desai, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that in respect of Sy.no.64/P10 of Kattugollahalli, Mandur Post, Biderhalli Hobli to an extent of 1 acre 20 guntas would also stand covered by decision in W.P.no.5389/2023.
With above observation, both writ petitions stand disposed of accordingly.
